# Can a one-check prediction market replicate on Jenkins?

## Registered before inspecting outcomes

Use Apache Karaf and Log4j, two separate open-source projects selected for locally manageable archive size. Neither contributed to the earlier ABB results. Join the archived Jenkins reports from Zenodo record 15603448 to the authors' metadata at commit `2c1b68e9b1d4ec6c4f304869e36af2e3168da889` using project, PR and build ID. A build may have several metadata rows for different stages; require agreement on its start timestamp and build duration. Count all unmatched files and metadata builds, empty reports and skipped tests. Reserve the first third by start time for practice only.

At a build's start, predict from only builds whose start plus duration precedes that instant. Release all of each such build's logged results together, settling forecasters in completion order. All policies may see the current roster of stage path, class and test name from the report, simulating a known manifest. Current status, skip indicators, duration, failure messages, file ordering, stage outcomes and commit text are unavailable to policies. Use only the first listed occurrence of a repeated identical identity, even when a later outcome disagrees. FIXED and PASSED count as passes, REGRESSION and FAILED as failures. A current skipped test can be chosen and yields no failure; do not train on skips or use them for log loss. Build failures in this study mean at least one first-record test failure.

Freeze the original four-expert equal blend, market, 32-build frequency and latest verdict. The two frequency forecasts inside the blend coincide before any check, exactly as for ABB. Wealth is per test, with the same 5% fixed share; a finished build updates the prevailing wealth using the forecasts made at its start. Include four-build recency, latest outcome of that identity from the same PR falling back to global latest, and a smoothed failure-rate baseline that shrinks each test toward the last 32 builds' pooled test failure probability using two pseudo-observations. Include expected uniform selection and an oracle. Break exact ties by the original smoothed frequency then lexical identity. Compare probability forecasts by mean per-build bits per *executed* test and the chosen first test by fraction of failing builds caught and fraction of all scored builds with a first-check catch. Record first-check hit on the subset with any prior completed build in the same PR. Report discordant builds for market versus equal. Use project-specific paired intervals from 4,000 PR-cluster bootstrap resamples and a 10-build moving-block sensitivity. Explicitly report small failure counts. The new practical promotion gate requires the market to gain at least five percentage points first-check hit rate on failing builds over equal shares, with positive lower PR-cluster bounds in each project, and beat the best simple control's point estimate in each. A first-check marketing claim fails if either project fails. The earlier 3-check primary ABB endpoint is separate.

[Dataset](https://zenodo.org/records/15603448) · [Build metadata](https://github.com/lrtsuser/LRTS/tree/2c1b68e9b1d4ec6c4f304869e36af2e3168da889/artifact/metadata)

## Verdict

The market and equal mixture found a failing test on their first check in the same **number** of builds in both projects. Five extra points did not replicate. Shrinking each test's observed failure frequency toward the project's historical base rate improved the first pick in both. The market improved probability estimates over the equal mixture, but the simple shrinkage rule also won on that metric. Both pre-probe blends give the 32-build frequency expert two identical forecasts.

| Project | Scored / failing builds | Market | Equal | Latest | Same-PR latest | Shrinkage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Karaf | 414 / 110 | 5 | 5 | 10 | 20 | **29** |
| Log4j | 180 / 72 | 38 | 38 | 39 | 40 | **42** |

Cells count builds where the first chosen test actually failed. On all builds, market hits were 1.21% and 21.11%, respectively. Conditional on a failure existing, the rates were 4.55% and 52.78%. The Karaf market rescued one equal-share miss and lost one equal-share hit. Its PR-cluster interval for the paired difference spanned −2.70 to +2.48 points. On Log4j every build had the same hit/miss in the two arms. Both resampling intervals there degenerated to [0,0]; resampling the observed builds cannot say how often an unseen project will disagree. The two arms picked exactly the same test in 407/414 and 177/180 builds, respectively. The market saved 0.0506 and 0.0505 bits per executed test relative to equal weights. The shrinkage comparator scored 0.0095 and 0.0017 bits, compared with the market's 0.0781 and 0.0758. The equal-to-market log-loss comparison by itself would substantially overstate the method's value.

The real failing answers were sparse: 301 failing identities among 368,814 executed first records on Karaf, and 352 among 1,137,987 on Log4j. With the original Beta(1,1) smoothing, unseen cases start at 50% predicted risk. Shrinkage uses the project's observed base rate and handles cold starts very differently. This is a candidate explanation for the ranking gap. The comparison changes a prior; it does not establish that all the gap occurred on cold starts.

All 620 Karaf and 270 Log4j metadata builds matched nonempty reports. The archive contained 106 and 43 further builds without metadata, respectively, excluded because they could not be placed on the same timeline. There were 2,454 and 289,329 repeated raw case occurrences across the matched builds, with 0 and 7 groups having conflicting statuses. The first occurrence determined the label. Reported skips were outside log loss and could yield a wasted selection; the chosen roster assumes access to a manifest of the tests that were eventually logged. A past build enters only after its documented finish time. First checks are retrospective recorded results and count tests rather than their runtime. The study does not distinguish defects from flaky tests or estimate effects of changing an actual CI schedule.

Run `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 python3 run.py` from this directory. The runner checks the metadata and archive digests, caches only the upstream archives in the user's cache, and contains a synthetic overlap check that flips unavailable outcomes and verifies first choices remain identical.
